PullRequest.Title: refactor(sessions): move sessions list drag and drop to sessionsListDragAndDrop.ts
PullRequest.Body:

## Why
Move 4 of phase 2 of splitting the 11.5k-line `sessionsList.ts` into smaller modules. Stacked on #349661.

## What changed
- Adds `sessionsListDragAndDrop.ts` with the Drag and Drop region, copied byte for byte: `SessionsListDragAndDrop`, its delegate and drop types, and its placement helpers.
- The only other edits: `export` added to the 16 declarations that `sessionsList.ts` still uses, the import lines of `sessionsList.ts` updated, and the region deleted from it. No other file imported these declarations, and nothing is re-exported.

## Scope
No behavior changes.

## Blast Radius
Only module load order changes. The moved code has no module-level side effects, the new module does not import `sessionsList.ts`, and no import cycle is introduced. The one moved `localize` call now belongs to `sessionsListDragAndDrop`, so language packs pick it up at the next translation pass.

## Verification
- Move check (a TypeScript compiler API script): all 257 top-level declaration blocks are identical at base and head, ignoring the 16 added `export` keywords.
- `typecheck-client`, `valid-layers-check`, `check-cyclic-dependencies` and `oxlint` on the changed files all pass.
- Unit tests for the sessions list and its importers, including `sessionsListChatMoveDnd.test.ts`: 6,992 tests, the same count as base.
- Component fixtures `sessionsList`, `sessionsListNotification`, `sessionsInboxScope` and `blockedSessionsList`: 346/346 screenshots identical to base.
- Bundled CSS for desktop, web, server-web and mobile: 6/6 files byte-identical.
- Code OSS Agents window, base and head: every grouping mode, Find, a context menu, drag and drop (including the drag-over feedback) and the blocked-sessions list give the same rows. All 12 screenshots are pixel-identical, and no new console errors appear.

Details in the first comment.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the sessions list and load the extracted drag-and-drop controller
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Module evaluation precedes list construction. sessionsList.ts still constructs and registers one SessionsListDragAndDrop instance at line 1158; the extracted module contains declarations, not eager service calls or controller construction.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One additional module per module-loader context, not one module per session, row, or drag event.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous declaration evaluation followed by the existing synchronous list/controller construction; no new async work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Normal module caching evaluates the new module once. Its dependencies were already imported by sessionsList.ts before the extraction; no new application cache, hydration, or negative-cache behavior is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: inspected both complete diffs, the new module imports and declarations, and the unchanged controller construction/ownership.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Bundler-specific module overhead and startup duration were not measured. There is no collection-scaling or heavyweight new initialization mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the extra module boundary relocates existing definitions without introducing expensive initialization or additional instances.

Scenarios.Scenario: Start and finish a drag of sessions or a nested chat
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Drag start synchronously resolves the dragged items, stores identifiers, and fills browser drag payloads. Drag end invokes the existing optional handler, clears transfers and dragged references, and resets feedback.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: JSON-encode session/chat identifiers and optional backend chat reference into browser DataTransfer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One payload for the first selected session, or one selected chat payload plus an optional reference; multi-session selection retains O(D) local identifiers but does not serialize every session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The deleted onDragStart body performed the same serialization and transfer updates; dnd.ts helpers are unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous on drag start, not repeated on every drag-over event.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: D selected sessions; finding a movable chat examines existing session/chat collections once at drag start for that controller's own chat drag.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous event callbacks. Optional drag-end opening is asynchronous and is not awaited before local transfer/reference cleanup.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The movable chat is resolved once into _draggedChat and reused on hover. Backend-resource lookup reads existing provider state; absent metadata does not initiate hydration. LocalSelectionTransfer remains the same singleton.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: added and deleted event bodies match, with unchanged delegate wiring and reference/payload helpers.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Selection sizes and serialized title/URI lengths are unmeasured; their costs and lifetimes are unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No new serialization amplification or retained-object lifetime: cleanup and per-drag caching are preserved.

Scenarios.Scenario: Hover drop targets, including expanded sessions, date sections, and group headers
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each drag-over event resolves the target and synchronously updates header, insertion, and row feedback before returning its reaction. Date placement validation can scan/sort existing session collections; nested targets can allocate feedback for visible descendant rows.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Find the hovered list row and read getBoundingClientRect to compute its quarter.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one geometry read per eligible drag-over/drop call with an event and list sector.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The identical getRowSector implementation was called at the same point by onDragOver and drop in sessionsList.ts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous browser geometry work before feedback updates.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Drag event frequency, selected-session count, existing sessions in the date/reorder scope, and visible nested rows; no provider request per row or hovered target.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serialized UI event callbacks; operation.run is invoked only on drop, so hover does not start provider moves or archive operations.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Own dragged-chat eligibility uses the drag-start cache; existing tree/model/provider metadata is read in memory. The extraction adds no invalidation or repeated cold lookup.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: full before/after resolver and helper comparison plus unchanged getSessionDropEffect, date validation, and tree delegates.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large date scopes may already cost significant CPU; no new traversal, sort, allocation, geometry read, or feedback update frequency is introduced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: existing hot-path work and geometry-read ordering are unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Drop sessions into pinned/custom/date placements, triage Inbox sessions, or reorder/nest headers
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A committed drop invokes the same list delegate, updates model/group state and sort keys, and notifies existing list consumers. Any required unarchive completes before membership changes. Inbox triage uses one command for the selected collection.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/browser/sessionGroupsService.ts:save, addToGroup, removeFromGroup, moveGroup; src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/browser/sessionsListModelService.ts:pinSession, unpinSessions, applySortChanges, setInboxState; src/vs/workbench/services/sessions/browser/sessionSectionOrderService.ts:reorder
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize changed group, pin, sort, inbox, or section-order state and submit it to profile storage.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Group joining and unpinning are batched; group removals and newly pinned sessions can save per changed session. Sort and inbox updates save their changed collection; a header drop performs a bounded number of group/order saves. No-op guards remain intact.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same resolver closures called the same moveSessions/moveHeader delegates, with identical batching, no-op guards, and storage call counts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Serialization and storage-service submission occur synchronously in the existing mutation path; physical storage flushing is owned by the unchanged storage subsystem.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: D changed selected sessions, persisted membership/pin/sort state, and G ordered headers/groups; pre-existing state serialization is not added or multiplied by the extraction.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Model/header mutations are synchronous; unarchive is sequential within one session-drop operation, and later group/order mutation waits for it. Inbox changes remain collection-batched.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing in-memory membership and pinned sets determine no-ops. Group save invalidates derived child IDs as before; no new retained cache or shadow state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: unchanged delegate wiring and list mutation methods traced into model/group/order persistence and Inbox action handlers.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Persisted state sizes and storage flush latency are unknown, but the PR does not change their call multiplicity or scheduling.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: existing potentially scaling persistence is pre-existing, not caused or amplified by moved types/helpers.

Scenarios.Scenario: Mark selected sessions done or restore archived sessions through a drop
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Archive drop runs one archive-with-undo command, cancels active requests, and awaits provider archive results before showing its undo notice. Restore awaits each selected archived session's provider unarchive before applying subsequent placement changes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Cancel active chat requests and send confirmed SessionIsArchivedChanged actions to the agent host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical archive command; sessions are grouped by provider. Agent-host batches still dispatch once per eligible session, not once per provider. Active-chat cancellation is conditional on active status.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The deleted resolver invoked the same moveSessions delegate, command, provider grouping, and limited archive dispatches.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cancellation completes before provider archiving; confirmed archive results precede the final undo notice.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Unarchive already archived selections via existing host dispatch; the experimental dev-container provider can reconnect its container and update detached-worktree state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider unarchive invocation per archived selected session. Agent-host unarchive submits one archive-state action; provider-specific connection work depends on the existing lifecycle state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Exactly the same selected archived-session loop and provider lifecycle paths were reached before extraction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Sequentially awaited before membership changes; base agent-host unarchive submits a dispatch without waiting for remote confirmation, while remote lifecycle work can delay the sequence.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: A eligible selected sessions, active chats within those sessions, and P provider groups; do not confuse P batches with A agent-host actions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Cancellation limiter is four sessions, with active chats sequential within a session. Provider batches run concurrently; each agent-host provider uses its existing shared limiter of four. Restore is sequential per drop.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Archive selection filters already archived sessions. Existing host session catalogs/subscriptions are reused; archive subscriptions are disposed in finally and pending notifications are batched/cleared. Dev-container warm/cold connection behavior is unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: archive command, management-service provider grouping/limiting, host dispatch/subscription lifecycle, and unarchive paths were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Remote provider and cold-container latency vary; the extraction preserves all provider operations, concurrency limits, and placement ordering.
Scenarios.Verdict: No introduced boundary fan-out, concurrency burst, or cleanup regression; operation counts and required ordering are unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Move/reorder a nested chat, promote it to a new session, or nest a single-chat session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Drop executes one runSessionsListMove call, which awaits one management/provider move. The host serializes moves, restores necessary cold session state, validates and commits catalog/folder changes, then existing move notifications allow list reveal.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Issue the existing moveChat request or session-move extension request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One move request per accepted single-chat/session drop; hover performs zero move requests and multi-chat/session drags do not fan out through this provider-move branch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The identical deleted run closures called the same delegates and one-request management/provider paths.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited by runSessionsListMove; successful reveal follows provider/catalog notifications.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read registration and catalog state, restore cold session data, prepare missing target working directories, and persist move-related catalog/configuration changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Work is scoped to the moved chat subtree and source/destination sessions. One cross-session catalog snapshot covers both sessions; missing directories are filtered against target folders and prepared sequentially. Reorder/promotion use their existing specialized branches.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same one-request drop path reached the same cold restoration, database reads, and folder preparation before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Host-side work must complete before its move request resolves; no work is moved into drag-over by this PR.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One dragged chat or single-chat session; moved chat subtree, session catalog size, and missing target directories control host work, not the whole list selection.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One request per accepted drop; all chat/session moves on a host share _chatMoveSequencer, and missing folders are prepared sequentially. Existing passive metadata sequencing and session leases remain unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Client eligibility/backend URIs use existing provider catalogs. Warm resident host sessions avoid restoration; cold sessions use existing in-flight/residency checks and move leases, released in finally. No extra metadata hydration or authoritative-state duplication.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: full resolver comparison, unchanged delegates, provider/protocol calls, host sequencer/restore/commit path, and existing one-call move tests inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cold restore duration and moved subtree/folder sizes are unmeasured; no scheduling, request-count, or retention change was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression or regression fix: provider/host work is relocated only at its client controller definition, not added, amplified, or eliminated.

Scenarios.Scenario: Drag a session/chat outside the main window to open an auxiliary chat window
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The unchanged drag-end helper invokes one registered handler. Eligible drag-outs await cursor/bounds resolution and then resolve/open the chat window; ordinary in-window drags fail the existing gates before opening.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Ask the existing host service for cursor screen coordinates/display to determine window bounds.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one request for an eligible single-session/chat drag-end; no call for ordinary rejected drag-outs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The deleted onDragEnd method invoked the same helper and handler with the same eligibility conditions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before opening the requested window; local drag-state cleanup does not await the handler.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve chat content and open an auxiliary window through auxiliaryWindowService.open, with existing editor transfer and window-owned UI construction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical open for an eligible dragged chat/session. Existing/canonical chat-window lookup reuses a window rather than opening another; a cold open constructs one auxiliary window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same existing window handler/service chain ran after the same drag-end callback before extraction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The drag-out workflow awaits resolution and window opening. Work remains post-drag and is not introduced onto list startup or hover.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One dragged chat/session and any editors transferred with it, not every selected list item.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Sequential bounds-then-open within one handler; no new callback registration, open loop, or concurrency multiplier.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing-window and resolved-canonical-window checks prevent duplicate window creation. Content/window/editor suppression disposables remain owned by existing services and cleanup paths.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: drag-end before/after comparison, singleton handler registration, drag-out gates, bounds request, and service reuse/creation paths inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Auxiliary-window creation and content restoration latency depend on platform/session state and were not measured; their placement and cardinality are unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: extraction preserves the optional handler, window reuse, and ownership/cleanup.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass for both files and every diff page against base 113482b1a8a4f6a71874425ed07a43e0e3f40a16. The controller, delegate types, and placement helpers are extracted with exports/import rewiring; executable bodies and controller ownership are unchanged. Traced startup, drag serialization/lifetime, hover/layout, placement/storage, archive/restore limiting, provider moves including cold host restoration, and auxiliary-window drag-out. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression and no concrete performance regression fix. Static review; runtime/bundler timings were not measured.
